_comment: The ONE table of cases for which wish tones are legal on which sentiment, read by BOTH
implementations: composeApp/src/commonTest/.../WishToneRulesTest.kt and
server/src/modules/wishes/tone-rules.spec.ts.
The rule exists twice, in two languages, because the server VALIDATES it on every draft
and on every history write, and the client HIDES the chips that are not offered. Neither
side can be dropped: a client that only hid the chips would let a tampered request
through, and a server that only validated would show the user a Funny button that 400s
on a death anniversary. MILESTONE_CHECKLIST.md §C is explicit about the price of that —
a rule implemented twice is held to one shared table of cases. The table is this file,
not a copy of it.
Six tones, not five. FR-WSH-03 lists the celebratory set (Warm, Funny, Respectful,
Short, Poetic) and FR-WSH-09 lists the solemn one (Respectful, Short, Heartfelt). They
overlap on two and HEARTFELT exists only on the solemn side, so neither is a subset of
the other and the union is six.
REQUIREMENTS.md §11 files 'no SOLEMN event can ever produce celebratory copy' under
correctness rather than content. The two rows marked expect:false on SOLEMN are
therefore the test that must go RED if somebody puts Funny or Poetic back —
docs/BUILD_PROMPT_M5.md, definition of done item 9.
Tone comes from the PERSON, never from the event type. A deceased person's birthday is a
SOLEMN event whose type is still BIRTHDAY, and M1 already got that wrong once — which is
why the last block below is keyed on (eventType, isDeceased) rather than on tone at all.

cases.why: the default, and the base case
FR-WSH-03. Shared with the solemn set
FR-WSH-03. Shared with the solemn set
FR-WSH-09 introduces HEARTFELT for the solemn composer only. FR-WSH-03's list does not contain it, so offering it on a birthday would be inventing a sixth celebratory tone nobody specified

THE ONE THAT MUST STAY RED. FR-WSH-09 makes Funny unavailable and REQUIREMENTS.md §11 files it under correctness: a joke on a death anniversary is the bug that gets an app uninstalled and screenshotted
the other half of FR-WSH-09's exclusion. Less obviously harmful than Funny and excluded for the same reason — the solemn set is a set you have to pick, not a filter applied afterwards
not in FR-WSH-09's list. 'Warm' is the celebratory default, and a default that leaked across would be the failure mode M1 had: the wrong set chosen because nobody chose

sentiment_cases.why: the type alone is enough. In practice creating one also sets is_deceased (FR-EVT-04), but the rule must not depend on the order those two writes land in

THE REMEMBRANCE BIRTHDAY, and the case M1 got wrong. The type is still BIRTHDAY. A composer that read tone off the event type would offer Funny and draft many happy returns for somebody who has died — FR-EVT-05 and REQUIREMENTS.md §7.3 call that the worst failure this product can have
a widow's wedding anniversary. Same shape as the remembrance birthday and easier to forget, because nothing in the type hints at it
anything owned by a deceased person is SOLEMN, whatever its type and whatever the user named it
